newsitem.title: HONG KONG: NatWest upbeat on post-Deng prospects for China.
newsitem.headline: NatWest upbeat on post-Deng prospects for China.

text.p: China still presents an attractive investment opportunity and economic prosperity will continue in the aftermath of the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, NatWest Markets said on Friday.
"The investment opportunities are still there," NatWest Markets economist Arthur Woo told Reuters.
The new leadership with President Jiang Zemin at its centre had "no choice" but to continue with the economic liberalisation programme started by Deng, Woo said.
In the company's latest research report issued on Thursday, Woo said investors must recognise that economic prosperity would continue in China.

"We believe that whoever becomes China's next long-term leader, whether it be Li Peng, Qiao Shi, Zhu Rongji, or any other dark horse, that leader will not turn back the clock on China's current economic reform programme," Woo wrote.
"For investors, that is the most important thing to recognise as China enters the 21st century. Economic prosperity will continue."
Although China was bound to undergo a certain amount of behind-the-scenes political manoeuvring, the majority of China's senior leaders were calling for national stability, Woo said in the report.
Jiang Zemin has inherited an economy due for a soft landing with consumer price growth at 8.3 percent in 1996, down from 17.1 percent in 1995, Woo said.
In the short term, China was unlikely to suffer the notorious boom and bust cycles of the past, as the non-state sector's output rose and the state sector output shrank, Woo wrote.
"Huge injections of foreign direct investment have helped lengthen the economic expansion and lowered cyclical volatility," Woo wrote.
Financial reforms had progressed significantly and central bank operations had become increasingly sophisticated, Woo wrote.
